fields.description:
## Problem
Reclaim/concurrency integration fixtures create bare repositories, then invoke Git with the bare repository as `cwd` but without an explicit `--git-dir`. On hosts configured with `safe.bareRepository=explicit`, fixture setup fails before test bodies run:

- `git config gc.autoDetach false` -> `fatal: not in a git directory` (exit 128)
- `git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/tickets` -> `fatal: cannot use bare repository ... (safe.bareRepository is 'explicit')` (exit 128)

The same errors reproduce from pristine `origin/main`; the failing tests import no force/transition/claim code. Linux CI currently uses Git defaults and therefore does not expose the failure, but the supported test suite must run both locally and in CI. Treat agents dismissing reproducible local test failures as environmental noise as an anti-pattern.

## Safety constraints
Be very cautious about Git configuration. Do not change, unset, or weaken host, global, system, or repository safety settings as remediation. Perform ticket and commit archaeology before proposing a fix so prior bare-repository safety fixes or contracts are not regressed. Prefer explicit, command-scoped repository targeting if the evidence supports it. Do not mask unrelated Git failures.

## Investigation plan
1. Inventory every affected reclaim/concurrency fixture command and the helper/call chain that creates and initializes bare repositories.
2. Search tickets and Git history for prior bare-repository, `safe.bareRepository`, `--git-dir`, fixture, and repository-isolation fixes; record the intended contracts and regression risks.
3. Reproduce from a fresh `origin/main` worktree using isolated command-scoped configuration that sets `safe.bareRepository=explicit`, without mutating host/global Git configuration. Include the default-config run as a negative control.
4. Use runtime evidence to confirm whether implicit repository discovery from a bare-repository `cwd` is the complete mechanism for both failures and rule out venv or product-code explanations.
5. After a proven RCA and legitimacy/caller-dependency checks, design a held-out RED oracle covering both failing command shapes and their observable fixture outcome.
6. Repair only the confirmed mechanism. Evaluate explicit `--git-dir` or an equivalent command-scoped invocation; do not change Git safety settings.
7. Prove GREEN, re-seed the exact defect to prove the oracle returns RED, and rerun the original report under both explicit-safe and default Git configurations.
8. Run focused reclaim/concurrency suites locally and through the normal CI matrix, plus lint/typecheck/complexity gates as applicable. Sweep semantically for sibling bare-repository commands using the same unsafe invocation pattern.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Exact affected fixture commands and call paths are inventoried with citations.
- [x] Relevant tickets and commits are archaeologically reviewed, with prior contracts and regression risks recorded.
- [x] The failure is reproduced on pristine `origin/main` using isolated command-scoped `safe.bareRepository=explicit`, without changing host/global Git settings.
- [x] A default-Git-config negative control demonstrates the environmental trigger while preserving the conclusion that local test portability is a repository responsibility.
- [x] A runtime-confirmed RCA explains both fixture setup failures and rules out venv and unrelated product-code causes.
- [x] A held-out final-form oracle is observed RED before the repair and covers both `git config` and `git symbolic-ref` bare-repository initialization paths.
- [x] The repair explicitly targets the bare repository (for example with `--git-dir`, if archaeology and experiments validate it) and does not weaken any Git safety setting.
- [x] The held-out oracle is GREEN after repair and returns RED when the exact implicit-discovery defect is reintroduced.
- [x] Focused reclaim/concurrency tests pass locally under both explicit-safe and default Git configurations and pass in the normal CI matrix.
- [x] Unrelated Git errors remain visible; no broad exception swallowing, retries, skips, xfails, or test weakening are introduced.
- [x] A semantic sibling sweep covers other bare-repository fixture invocations and dispositions every confirmed instance.
